Polya-Aeppli Distribution

Source: R/paeppli.R
PolyaAeppli.Rd

Density, distribution function, quantile function, and random generation for the Polya-Aeppli (Poisson-geometric) distribution.

Usage

dpaeppli(x, lambda, prob, log = FALSE)

ppaeppli(q, lambda, prob, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)

qpaeppli(p, lambda, prob, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)

rpaeppli(n, lambda, prob)

Arguments

x

vector of (non-negative integer) quantiles.

lambda

vector of (non-negative) Poisson rates \(\lambda\) of clusters.

prob

vector of geometric parameters \(0 \leq q < 1\): each cluster has \(c \geq 1\) events with probability \((1 - q) q^{c - 1}\).

log, log.p

logical; if TRUE, probabilities p are given as log(p).

q

vector of quantiles.

lower.tail

logical; if TRUE (default), probabilities are \(P(Y \leq y)\), otherwise \(P(Y > y)\).

p

vector of probabilities.

n

number of observations. If length(n) > 1, the length is taken to be the number required.

Value

dpaeppli gives the probability mass, ppaeppli the distribution function, qpaeppli the quantile function, and rpaeppli random deviates. The length of the result is determined by n for rpaeppli, and is the maximum of the lengths of the numerical arguments for the other functions.

Details

A Polya-Aeppli random variable is a Poisson number of clusters with geometric cluster sizes: $$Y = \sum_{i = 1}^{M} C_i, \quad M \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda), \quad P(C_i = c) = (1 - q) q^{c - 1}, \; c = 1, 2, \ldots$$ so that \(P(Y = 0) = e^{-\lambda}\) and, for \(y \geq 1\), $$P(Y = y) = e^{-\lambda} \sum_{j = 1}^{y} \frac{\lambda^j}{j!} \binom{y - 1}{j - 1} q^{y - j} (1 - q)^j.$$ The mean and variance are $$E[Y] = \frac{\lambda}{1 - q}, \qquad \mathrm{Var}[Y] = \frac{\lambda (1 + q)}{(1 - q)^2}.$$ \(q = 0\) gives the Poisson distribution with mean \(\lambda\). The parameterization is that of the polyaAeppli package.

The Polya-Aeppli distribution is the Poisson-Tweedie distribution with power parameter 1.5: a count with mean \(\mu\) and variance \(\mu + \phi\mu^{1.5}\) is Polya-Aeppli with \(q = d / (2 + d)\) and \(\lambda = \mu (1 - q)\), where \(d = \phi\sqrt{\mu}\).

Probabilities are computed by summing the decomposition over the number of clusters on the log scale (all terms are positive); both tails are computed directly. Random deviates are generated from the definition.

References

Johnson, N. L., Kemp, A. W. and Kotz, S. (2005). Univariate Discrete Distributions (3rd ed.), Section 9.7. Wiley.

Bonat, W. H., Jorgensen, B., Kokonendji, C. C., Hinde, J. and Demetrio, C. G. B. (2018). Extended Poisson-Tweedie: properties and regression models for count data. Statistical Modelling, 18(1), 24-49.

Examples

dpaeppli(0:6, lambda = 2, prob = 0.3)
#> [1] 0.13533528 0.18946940 0.18946940 0.15852273 0.11829206 0.08134174 0.05255308
# prob = 0 gives the Poisson distribution
all.equal(dpaeppli(0:10, lambda = 2, prob = 0), dpois(0:10, 2))
#> [1] TRUE
ppaeppli(4, lambda = 2, prob = 0.3)
#> [1] 0.7910889
qpaeppli(c(0.5, 0.95), lambda = 2, prob = 0.3)
#> [1] 2 7
set.seed(7)
y <- rpaeppli(5000, lambda = 2, prob = 0.3)
c(mean = mean(y), var = var(y))   # theory: 2.857 and 5.306
#>     mean      var 
#> 2.860200 5.362128
